classification.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the perpendicular radius to obtain the tangent gradient, using the contact point for its equation, and recognising that the inscribed circle's diameter equals the square's side. The parts separate these familiar connections; the source diagram's inconsistent axis placements do not constitute an additional intended reasoning demand.

content.prompt: The circle to the right has equation $x^2+y^2=25$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8, shared diagram to the right of parts a–d
spec.description: Unshaded coordinate diagram: the circle x^2+y^2=25 centred at the origin, the circumscribed square ABCD with A(7,1), B(-1,7), C(-7,-1), D(1,-7) tangent to the circle at (3,4), (-4,3), (-3,-4) and (4,-3), the two perpendicular diameters and right-angle marks. Ordinary source blue geometry and red point markers use black. The origin label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: The tangents at (3,4), (-4,3), (-3,-4) and (4,-3) are 3x+4y=25, -4x+3y=25, -3x-4y=25 and 4x-3y=25; consecutive tangents meet at A(7,1), B(-1,7), C(-7,-1) and D(1,-7). AB = 10, so the square has side 10 (the circle diameter) and area 100.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied labels and relationships are shown; no calculated gradients, equations, lengths or areas are printed.

answer.worked:
The radius to $(3,4)$ is perpendicular to $AB$.
$$\begin{align*}m_{\text{radius}}&=\frac{4-0}{3-0}\\m_{\text{radius}}&=\frac43\\m_{AB}&=-\frac{1}{4/3}\\m_{AB}&=-\frac34\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the equation of the line $AB$.

answer.short:
$10$ units.

For the stated square, its side equals the diameter of the inscribed circle.
answer.worked:
The circle is inscribed in the stated square, so its diameter equals the side length.
$$\begin{align*}r^2&=25\\r&=5\\AB&=2r\\AB&=10\end{align*}$$
Thus $AB=10$ units.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the area of the square $ABCD$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }ABCD&=AB^2\\\text{Area of }ABCD&=10^2\\\text{Area of }ABCD&=100\end{align*}$$
The area is $100$ square units.
